scope: Design acceptance only for restoring the actual sibling app checkout and dependencies in the two content verification workflows. No implementation, hosted CI, release, external publication, native, or full BIZQ-01 acceptance is claimed.
decisiveReasons: The CI failure is an actual ENOENT at the existing admission API's sibling path, reproduced by the saved missing-input probe before any receipt write.
The proposed sibling directories match the existing test's resolve(root, '../patternly') contract; the first checkout must therefore use path patternly-content and the second path patternly.
A validated full SHA from the committed admission pins checkout to the admitted frontend commit rather than a moving branch; the exact commit exists and is currently reachable from app origin/main.
Both repositories are public, so the fixed cross-repository checkout does not require a new secret or service configuration. Node 22 and npm ci align with the existing workflows and app engine range.
The proposal retains existing triggers and all checks, does not dispatch manual release, and does not modify admission semantics or the no-deployment boundary.
The candidate draft source identity is derived from content paths, so workflow-only changes do not change the content source snapshot identity.
implementationClarifications: Place the initial content checkout in GITHUB_WORKSPACE/patternly-content; otherwise the proposed sibling layout is not realized.
Keep run steps rooted in patternly-content and point the manual workflow's cache-dependency-path at patternly-content/package-lock.json.
Validate frontendCommit as exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters before publishing it as a step output and using it for the fixed app repository checkout.
limits: No workflow implementation or hosted CI result is accepted by this review; post-push content CI must actually complete the existing build/readiness steps.
No release readiness, deployment, external publication, native/Premium, or full BIZQ-01 completion is claimed.
